# Introduction

We can use two sequences as querys to extract the genes from our
samples. The first is to download one COI and lsrDNA sequences 
from GenBank. The second is to use the extracted genes from the 
draft genome we assembled.

Additionally, we construct two phylogenetic trees to see the
relationships between the samples.

## Getting the sequences from GenBank
Since we expect to have *C. farionis* in our samples, we used its
available markers for COI and lrsDNA. 

```{bash, collapse=TRUE}
# From ENA:
if [ ! -d markers ];then mkdir markers; fi
if [ ! -e acc_COI.txt ]; then
   PORTAL="https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/portal/api/search?"
   RESULT="result=sequence&"
   QUERY="query=accession=MW729433&"
   FIELDS="fields=accession%2Cscientific_name&"
   FORMAT="format=tsv"
   curl -s $PORTAL$RESULT$QUERY$FIELDS$FORMAT | \
   cut -f 1 | tail -n +2 > acc_COI.txt
fi
BROWSER="https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/browser/api/fasta/"
ACCESSION=$(gawk -v ORS="," '{print}' acc_COI.txt | sed 's/.$//' | cut -d ',' -f 1)
if [ ! -e markers/$ACCESSION.fa ]; then 
  curl -s $BROWSER$ACCESSION > markers/$ACCESSION.fa
  sed -i "/>/c >${ACCESSION}_Cfarionis_COI" markers/${ACCESSION}.fa
fi

if [ ! -e acc_28S.txt ]; then
   PORTAL="https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/portal/api/search?"
   RESULT="result=sequence&"
   QUERY="query=accession=MW368674&"
   FIELDS="fields=accession%2Cscientific_name&"
   FORMAT="format=tsv"
   curl -s $PORTAL$RESULT$QUERY$FIELDS$FORMAT | \
   cut -f 1 | tail -n +2 > acc_28S.txt
fi
BROWSER="https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/browser/api/fasta/"
ACCESSION=$(gawk -v ORS="," '{print}' acc_28S.txt | sed 's/.$//' | cut -d ',' -f 1)
if [ ! -e markers/$ACCESSION.fa ]; then 
  curl -s $BROWSER$ACCESSION > markers/$ACCESSION.fa
  sed -i "/>/c >${ACCESSION}_Cfarionis_28S" markers/${ACCESSION}.fa
fi
 rm *.txt
```

# Mapping of ddRAD-seq reads to *cox1* and *lsrDNA* genes

I'm going to test several COI markers obtained from GenBank, Isabel or our assemblies. We don't know if 
there are three species in our samples, so I'm going to test the COI from C. farionis and 
C. pseudofarionis. Since the same gene can not be mapped at the same time, I need to create a specific 
folder for each marker. At the end, I'm gonna leave the code in README, but without executation, only 
keeping the chosen marker. 

## Creating the REF file 
List of COI sequences for C. farionis and C. pseudofarionis
* COI_Cfar - ExKD25_21_TA2003_AC_Cfar (Isa)
* COI_Cpse - ExKD8_7_TA2018_BT_Cpse (Isa)
* COI_MW - GenBank sequence from Russia 
* Cox1_Cpse_ONT - Cox1 extracted from the assembly of C.pseudofarionis 
* Cox1_Cfar_ASM - Cox1 extracted from the assembly of C.farionis

```{bash}
if [ ! -e markers/COI_Cfar.fa ]; then cat markers/ExKD25_21_TA2003_AC_Cfar.fa > markers/COI_Cfar.fa \
      && sed -i '1s/.*/>COI_Cfar/' markers/COI_Cfar.fa; fi
if [ ! -e markers/COI_Cpse.fa ]; then cat markers/ExKD8_7_TA2018_BT_Cpse.fa > markers/COI_Cpse.fa \
      && sed -i '1s/.*/>COI_Cpse/' markers/COI_Cpse.fa; fi
if [ ! -e markers/COI_MW.fa ]; then cat markers/MW729433.fa > markers/COI_MW.fa \
      && sed -i '1s/.*/>COI_MW/' markers/COI_MW.fa; fi
if [ ! -e markers/Cox1_Cfar_ASM.fa ]; then cat ../2023-06-22/Cox1Ref.fa > markers/Cox1_Cfar_ASM.fa \
      && sed -i '1s/.*/>Cox1_Cfar_ASM/' markers/Cox1_Cfar_ASM.fa; fi
if [ ! -e markers/Cox1_Cpse_ONT.fa ]; then cat Cox1_Cpse_ONT_Ref.fa > markers/Cox1_Cpse_ONT.fa \
      && sed -i '1s/.*/>Cox1_Cpse_ONT/' markers/Cox1_Cpse_ONT.fa; fi

if [ ! -e markers/lsrDNA_MW.fa ]; then cat markers/MW368674.fa > markers/lsrDNA_MW.fa \
      && sed -i '1s/.*/>lsrDNA_MW/' markers/lsrDNA_MW.fa; fi
if [ ! -e markers/lsrDNA_Cfar.fa ]; then cat ../2023-06-22/lsrDNARef.fa > markers/lsrDNA_Cfar.fa \
      && sed -i '1s/.*/>lsrDNA_Cfar/' markers/lsrDNA_Cfar.fa; fi

```

```{bash}

PATHFQ=../2023-05-17/crepi_edits

for REF in COI_Cfar COI_Cpse COI_MW Cox1_Cfar_ASM Cox1_Cpse_ONT lsrDNA_MW lsrDNA_Cfar; do
  if [ ! -d BAM_$REF ]; then mkdir BAM_$REF; fi
  if [ ! -e markers/$REF.0123 ]; then
     bwa-mem2 index markers/${REF}.fa
  fi

  #bwa-mem2 index $COX
  for i in $(ls $PATHFQ/*.trimmed_R1_.fastq.gz); do
     SAMPLE=$(basename $i .trimmed_R1_.fastq.gz)
     if [ ! -e BAM_$REF/${SAMPLE}.bam ]; then
        if [ ! -e BAM_$REF/${SAMPLE}.sam ]; then
           # I skip "pairing" (-P) and avoid "mate rescue" (-S), to map forward
           # and reverse reads independently.
           bwa-mem2 mem -t 24 -P -S markers/${REF}.fa ${PATHFQ}/${SAMPLE}.trimmed_R1_.fastq.gz \
                                   ${PATHFQ}/${SAMPLE}.trimmed_R2_.fastq.gz \
                        -R "@RG\tID:${SAMPLE}\tSM:${SAMPLE}" > BAM_$REF/${SAMPLE}.sam &
        fi
        wait
        # We expect very few reads to map on cox1 or lsrDNA, and don't need to
        # save the rest in the bam. Thus, I filter the umapped reads.
        samtools view -q 20 -F 4 -u BAM_$REF/${SAMPLE}.sam | \
        samtools sort > BAM_$REF/${SAMPLE}.bam
        samtools index BAM_$REF/${SAMPLE}.bam
        rm BAM_$REF/${SAMPLE}.sam
     fi
  done
done
```

## Extract a consensus sequences for each BAM file 
List of COI sequences for C. farionis and C. pseudofarionis
* COI_Cfar - ExKD25_21_TA2003_AC_Cfar (Isa)
* COI_Cpse - ExKD8_7_TA2018_BT_Cpse (Isa)
* COI_MW - GenBank sequence from Russia 
* Cox1_Cpse_ONT - Cox1 extracted from the assembly of C.pseudofarionis 
* Cox_Cfar_ASM - Cox1 extracted from the assembly of C.farionis
* lsrDNA_MW.fa - GenBank sequence from Russia
* lsrDNA_Cfar.fa - lsrDNA extracted from the assembly of C.farionis


```{bash}

for REF in COI_Cfar COI_Cpse COI_MW Cox1_Cfar_ASM Cox1_Cpse_ONT lsrDNA_MW lsrDNA_Cfar; do
  if [ ! -e ${REF}_align.fa ]; then
    for bam in $(ls -1 BAM_$REF/*.bam); do
      SAMPLE=$(basename -s .bam $bam)
      samtools consensus -r $REF $bam -A --P-het 0 \
                         -l 2000 -a --show-del yes --show-ins no | \
      sed "s/>${REF}/>${SAMPLE}/" | \
      sed "s/*/-/g" >> ${REF}_align.fa
    done
  fi
done

```

The samples are: T165Cxa, N048Cma, N048Cmb, N048Cmc, N044Cx2

## Phylogenetic reconstruction

```{bash eval=FALSE}
if [ ! -d RAxML ]; then mkdir RAxML; fi
```

```{r eval=FALSE}
writeXStringSet(readDNAStringSet('COI_Cfar_align.fa')[grep("L|S", names(readDNAStringSet('COI_Cfar_align.fa')))], "GB/COI_Cfar_align.fa")
writeXStringSet(readDNAStringSet('COI_Cpse_align.fa')[grep("L|S", names(readDNAStringSet('COI_Cpse_align.fa')))], "GB/COI_Cpse_align.fa")
writeXStringSet(readDNAStringSet('COI_MW_align.fa')[grep("L|S", names(readDNAStringSet('COI_MW_align.fa')))], "GB/COI_MW_align.fa")
writeXStringSet(readDNAStringSet('Cox1_Cfar_ASM_align.fa')[grep("L|S", names(readDNAStringSet('Cox1_Cfar_ASM_align.fa')))], "GB/Cox1_Cfar_ASM_align.fa")
writeXStringSet(readDNAStringSet('Cox1_Cpse_ONT_align.fa')[grep("L|S", names(readDNAStringSet('Cox1_Cpse_ONT_align.fa')))], "GB/Cox1_Cpse_ONT_align.fa")
writeXStringSet(readDNAStringSet('lsrDNA_MW_align.fa')[grep("L|S", names(readDNAStringSet('lsrDNA_MW_align.fa')))], "GB/lsrDNA_MW_align.fa")
writeXStringSet(readDNAStringSet('lsrDNA_Cfar_align.fa')[grep("L|S", names(readDNAStringSet('lsrDNA_Cfar_align.fa')))], "GB/lsrDNA_Cfar_align.fa")
```

```{bash eval = FALSE}
for A in COI_Cfar_align.fa; do
  BASENAME=$(basename -s .fa $A)
  gawk '(/^>/){
     print $0
  }(/^[^>]/){
     gsub(/N/, "-", $1)
     print $1
  }' $A > GB/${BASENAME}_noN.fasta
done
```

Filter and trim the alignments with Gblocks 
```{bash eval=FALSE}
for COI in COI_Cfar_align.fa COI_Cfar_align.fa COI_Cpse_align.fa COI_MW_align.fa Cox1_Cfar_ASM_align.fa Cox1_Cpse_ONT_align.fa; then 
  if [ ! -e GB/$COI-gb1 ]; then
     Gblocks GB/$COI -t=d -b1=46 -b2=60 -b4=10 -e=-gb1 -d=y -v=1000 -b3=10 -b5=h
  fi
done

for lsrDNA in lsrDNA_MW_align.fa lsrDNA_Cfar_align.fa; then 
  if [ ! -e GB/$lsrDNA-gb1 ]; then
     Gblocks GB/$lsrDNA -t=d -b1=59 -b2=91 -b4=10 -e=-gb1 -d=y -v=1000 -b3=50 -b5=h
  fi
done

```

Since all the markers of COI maps aprox. the same name of sequences, 
that are very low in all cases, we choose the marker extracted of our 
reference genome of *C.farionis* (short reads). For lsrDNA, the sequences 
aligned with the markers are so much more long, and the mapping is again 
very similar between the markers tested, so we choose the lsrDNA extracted 
of the *C.farionis* assembly.
